item.title: Presented Research at JSM 2026
item.description:
Joint Statistical Meetings 2026

I had the opportunity to present my research at the 2026 Joint Statistical Meetings (JSM) in Boston, Massachusetts.

This conference brought together statisticians from academia, industry, and government to discuss recent advances in statistics and biostatistics.

Poster Presentation

I presented the poster

Adaptive Weighting for Time-to-Event Continual Reassessment Method: Improving Safety in Phase I Dose-Finding Trials

The work introduces an adaptive predictive weighting approach that reduces overdosing while maintaining accurate maximum tolerated dose (MTD) selection.

Key Findings

  • 40.6% reduction in overdosing
  • Maintained MTD selection accuracy
  • Drop-in replacement for the standard TITE-CRM
  • Applicable to Phase I oncology trials

Standing beside my poster during the JSM poster session.

Research Impact

This work addresses one of the major challenges in Phase I oncology trials: delayed toxicity.

Instead of relying on fixed linear follow-up weights, the proposed method uses adaptive predictive weights based on observed toxicity timing, improving patient safety while preserving trial efficiency.

The manuscript is currently under review at Statistics in Medicine.

Related Research

  • Adaptive TITE-CRM Project

Looking Ahead

The same research will be presented at the

Statistics in Pharmaceuticals (SIP) 2026

conference later this month.

I look forward to discussing the methodology with researchers working in adaptive clinical trial design and Bayesian biostatistics.
